Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by D.I. Crawford.

Enquiries show that Mrs Selina F. ROSLING
resided at 101 Route Vallon from 16.5.40 to 31.10.40
when she removed to another address , which has so far
not been ascertained.

Vallon, so that she is bound to call for them shortly.
The landlord has been approached in a discreet manner
with the request to obtain from Mrs Rosling her present
address.

this person's whereabouts are ascertained, a report will
be submitted.

BRITISH CONSULATE-GENERAL,
SHANGHAI.

29th October 1940.

Dear Mr. Robertson,

Your letter D. 6608 of the 3rd April 1940.

I should be grateful if you could ascertain
by discreet inquiries whether Mrs. Galina ROSLING is
still living at Apartment 5, No.101 Route Vallon, Shanghai.

I don't want to see the lady, who is the most
insistent and almost the most unintelligible talker I've
met.

Many thanks for your kindness in keeping me
informed on these matters.

Yours sincerely,

Passport Control Officer.

H. D. M. Robertson, Esquire,
Assistant Commissioner,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
SHANGHAI.

D. S. J. Polokoff

about me as it seems - that my husband Arthur Rosling had informed

Mrs. Galina Pavlovna ROSLING left Shanghai for Kobe
on November 9, 1938 in the s.s. "Suwa Maru." Enquiries show
that on or about November 4 she booked third class single
passage to San Francisco, Cal., U.S.A., and that she intended
to continue her voyage from Japan in the s.s. "Tatuta Maru"
which was scheduled to sail from Kobe on November 12, 1938.

Particulars of a declaration form filled in by
Mrs. Rosling when booking passage at the local office of
the N.Y.K. Line are as follows :-

Galina Pavlovna ROSLING 夫人于1938年11月9日乘坐“苏瓦丸”号轮船（s.s. "Suwa Maru"）离开上海前往神户。经查，她大约在11月4日预订了前往美国加利福尼亚州旧金山的单程三等舱船票，并打算从日本继续行程，乘坐预定于1938年11月12日从神户启航的“龙田丸”号轮船（s.s. "Tatuta Maru"）。

Rosling 夫人在日本邮船会社（N.Y.K. Line）本地办事处预订船票时填写的申报单详情如下：

姓名：Galina P. Rosling 夫人
年龄：26岁
家庭状况：已婚
职业：家庭主妇
国籍：英国
种族：俄罗斯人
出生地：俄罗斯莫斯科。
签证：1938年2月5日在新加坡海峡殖民地签发的移民签证第135号
最后永久居住地：新加坡海峡殖民地。
近亲：丈夫 - A.K. Rosling 先生，英王陛下部队（Barisa，靠近新加坡海峡殖民地？）
最终目的地：加利福尼亚州旧金山。
旅行目的：探望姐姐 O. Smith 夫人，地址转交加州旧金山海军医院。
拟停留时间：2 - 3个月。
外貌描述：身高5英尺3英寸，肤色白皙，浅棕色头发，蓝眼睛，无标记。

26th October, 1933.

Dear Heaney,

Last August you sent me copy of a report from
Section One of the Special Branch of the Municipal Police
regarding Mrs. G.P. Rosling, nee Morasova. In this report
it says that she arrived in Shanghai from Manila on August
15th in the s.s. "Conte Biancamano" and that her address
was not then available. I shall be grateful if you will
be so good as to ask the Police for any further information
that may have come to light regarding this woman's where-
abouts and activities.

Yours sincerely,

R.S. Heaney, Esquire, M.B.E.,
British Consulate-General,

April 30th, 1938.

Sir,

I would be greatly obliged if you would kindly forward
to me the address of my wife Mrs. Galina Rosling, I given to
understand that she is now living in Shanghai.

My wife left Tientsin on December 23rd, 1937 on her own
accord, I had given her my consent previously to take a holiday
at Hong-Kong and I informed her that she should let me make
the necessary arrangements for her passage to Hong-Kong as
being a soldier's wife she could travel Military rate, I
made enquiries for her at Butterfield & Swires Offices at
Tientsin and made arrangements for her to see the person
concerned at that office. In the meantime she must have made
arrangements unknown to me elsewhere as she sailed unknown to me
on the " SS TAKSANG" owned by the "China Navigation Company".

As my duty kept me away from my wife from 7:30 a.m. until
7:30 p.m. I was quite unaware that she had any intentions of
going away on the day she went December 23rd.1938. When I
arrived home from duty at 7:30 p.m. on December 23rd, my wife
was not at home and I found a note saying that she was sorry
that she had had to go away in such a hurry as the ship she was
sailing on was leaving earlier than she had expected and if she
did not sail on that particular ship she would lose her passage
money, she also stated that she had sailed on a Japanese ship
and had gone to Hong-Kong and would be away from Tientsin for
one month only. On January 12th.1938. I received a letter
from my wife from Shanghai dated January 6th 1938. stating that
/she

先生：

    如蒙惠示我妻子加利娜·罗斯林夫人的地址，我将不胜感激，据我了解她目前居住在上海。

    我妻子于1937年12月23日自行离开天津，此前我已同意她去香港度假，并告知她应由我来为她安排赴港船票，因为作为军人家属，她可享受军运票价。我在天津的太古洋行（Butterfield & Swires）办事处为她进行了查询，并安排她与该行相关人员会面。与此同时，她必定在其他地方瞒着我做了安排，因为她瞒着我登上了“中国航业公司”（China Navigation Company）所属的“德兴轮”（SS TAKSANG）。

    由于我的职责使我从早上7:30到晚上7:30都无法陪伴妻子，所以在1938年12月23日她离开的那天，我完全不知道她有离开的意图。当我于1938年12月23日晚上7:30下班回家时，妻子不在家，我发现一张纸条，说她很抱歉如此匆忙离去，因为她乘坐的船只比预期提前离港，如果她不搭乘那班船，就会损失船费；她还说她已乘一艘日本船只前往香港，只离开天津一个月。1938年1月12日，我收到妻子从上海寄来的信，日期为1938年1月6日，信中称/她

page_data.en:
2.
she was sailing from Shanghai the next day for Paris and England
and that her relations at Paris had sent her the money for her
passage, I consulted the shipping notices to see if it had been
possible for her to sail and I found that it not possible for
her to leave Shanghai that day. At the same time I made
enquiries at all the Shipping Companies in Tientsin to see by
what boat she had left Tientsin by and as I have stated above
she sailed on the "SS TAKSANG" travelling 1st class Chinese
passage without food 45 (Dollars) and that she had booked her
passage to Shanghai and not Hong-Kong.
I informed my Officer Commanding about the matter at once
and the matter was placed in the hands of the British Municipal
Police who obtained all the necessary information they required
about my wife from myself, I have not yet received any informa
tion from the police as regards the where-a-bouts of my wife.
On February 19th 1938 the "SS TAKSANG" arrived at
Tientsin Bund, and I decided to enquire from the ship's officers
if they could remember my wife travelling on the ship on its
journey to Shanghai and Hong-Kong. The Purser Mr. Ward was
the only one who remembered her, I informed him of the object
of my enquiries and he kindly volunteered to do anything he
could to assist me in any way during his return journey to
Shanghai. I asked him to ascertain if my wife was still in
Shanghai and I gave him a letter to deliver to her personally,
the "SS TAKSANG" sailed from Tientsin on February 21st. 1938.
When the ship returned to Tientsin again I again saw Mr. Ward
and he informed me that he had been to the Consular Offices
at Shanghai to ascertain the address of my wife and that the
Consular staff informed him that it was against the regulations
to give him the address but he was told that if he left the
letter it would be forwarded on to my wife since the letter
has been delivered I have not yet received any answer.
With a view of coming to Shanghai myself to attend to the
matter I would be greatly obliged if you would forward me her
/address

她将于次日从上海启程前往巴黎和英国，她在巴黎的亲属已寄给她船费。我查阅了航运公告，看她是否有可能成行，结果发现她当天不可能离开上海。同时，我向天津的所有轮船公司查询她是乘哪艘船离开天津的，正如我上述所言，她是乘坐“德兴轮”（SS TAKSANG），购买的是不含膳食的一等华籍乘客票，票价45（美元），且她预订的是去上海的船票，而非香港。

    我立即将此情况报告了我的指挥官，此事随后交由英工部局警务处处理，他们从我这里获取了关于我妻子所需的所有必要信息，但至今我尚未收到警方关于我妻子下落的任何消息。1938年2月19日，“德兴轮”抵达天津外滩，我决定向船方官员询问，他们是否记得我妻子在该船前往上海和香港的航程中同行。只有大副沃德先生（Mr. Ward）记得她，我向他说明了我的查询目的，他好心地表示愿意在返回上海的途中尽力协助我。我请他查明我妻子是否仍在上海，并交给他一封信，请他亲自转交。“德兴轮”于1938年2月21日从天津启航。当该船再次返回天津时，我又见到了沃德先生，他告诉我他曾去上海的领事馆办公室查询我妻子的地址，但领事馆工作人员告诉他，按规定不能提供地址，不过被告知如果留下信件，将会转交给我妻子。既然信已送达，但我至今仍未收到回复。

    为了亲自前往上海处理此事，如蒙惠示其/地址

3.
address and if possible that she will not be allowed to leave
the port until I ascertained her intentions.
I am
Sir,
Your Obedient
Driver R.A.S.C.
(Signed) A ROSLING.

Dear Sir,

    I forward herewith the information required by you re GALINA MIKLOVA MORASOVA nee VLASOVA.

    The actual date of her arrival in China is unknown but according to her own statement she escaped across the border near Pogranichnaya, being the only survivor of the party that attempted that escape from Soviet Russia. She then stayed in Harbin where she was employed as a milliner, but upon her appearance in Harbin it was rumoured that she was an agent of the G.P.U. Her exact date of arrival in Tientsin is unknown but shortly after her arrival in Tientsin she was living with a French Military Sergeant (Artillery) name unknown.

    In about April, 1936, Morasova commenced to live with an American Radio Sergeant attached to the 15th Infantry named SHENDON or SHELDON, from whom, it is alleged, she obtained information which she supplied to the local Soviet Consulate. After co-habiting with him for 10 months they quarrelled and Morasova left for Hankow, but, however, soon returned to Tientsin and stayed at 309 Race Course Road. This was about 10th April, 1937.

    Sheldon patched up their quarrel and continued to visit her there for a short period as in May, 1937, he was sent back to America.

亲爱的先生：

    兹转呈您所需的关于 GALINA MIKLOVA MORASOVA，婚前姓 VLASOVA 的信息。

    她抵达中国的确切日期不详，但据其自称，她是试图从苏俄越境逃亡的一伙人中唯一的幸存者，在波格拉尼奇纳亚（Pogranichnaya）附近越过边境。随后她留在哈尔滨，受雇为帽商，但在她出现在哈尔滨后，有传言称她是国家政治保卫总局（G.P.U.）的特工。她抵达天津的确切日期不详，但在抵达天津后不久，她便与一名法国军队中士（炮兵）同居，姓名不详。

    大约在1936年4月，莫拉索娃（Morasova）开始与隶属于第15步兵团的一名美国无线电中士 SHENDON 或 SHELDON 同居，据称她从该人处获取情报并提供给当地苏联领事馆。在与他同居10个月后，两人发生争吵，莫拉索娃前往汉口，但不久又返回天津，住在跑马厅路309号。这大约是1937年4月10日。

    谢尔登（Sheldon）与她和好，并在短时间内继续去那里探望她，直到1937年5月他被遣返美国。

                                                                于

page_data.en:
3
2.
On the 30th or 31st May, 1937, Morasova left
for Chefoo with a certain woman NINA MOSOLNIK, a Russian
who was living with an American N.C.O. of the 15th Infantry
named MILLS who had also left for America. The last
address known of this soldier is, W.H. Mills, Box 506,
Gaffney, South Carolina. After staying in Chefoo for about
one month Morasova returned to Tientsin and lived in a
Chinese boarding house in Oxford Road. While she was
staying at 309, Race Course Road she became friendly with
the wife of an American Medical Officer named Ford, who
together with the whole family left for Manila on the 3rd
July, 1937. Morasova continued correspondence with Mrs.
Ford and later informed people that Mrs. Ford had been
divorced in Manila and had proceeded to Singapore and had
invited her to stay with her for a time. Several times
Morasova stated that she intended to go to Singapore and
visit Mrs. Ford. During the whole of her stay in
Tientsin Morasova was not employed in any capacity yet
always appeared to be in funds. It was during her stay
at the boarding house in Oxford Road that she became
acquainted with Private Rosling. At the beginning of the
local hostilities Morasova was very nervous and continually
expressed her fear, (quite easily understood if she was
working for G.P.U.)
On September 6, 1937 she married Rosling at the
Russian church, no registration at the Consulate being
made but full details were registered with the British
Military. Her age given at the time of marriage was 25.
After the wedding she quite freely said that now she had
nothing to fear as she was a British Subject and held a
British Passport, and openly boasted that she married
Rosling for that purpose; i.e. to get a British Passport.
As already know Mrs. Rosling left Tientsin on the
/27th
page_data.zh:
3
2.
1937年5月30日或31日，莫拉索娃与一位名叫尼娜·莫索尔尼克（NINA MOSOLNIK）的俄国女子一同前往烟台，该女子当时与第15步兵团一名名叫米尔斯（MILLS）的美国士官同居，米尔斯也已返回美国。这名士兵已知的最后地址是：W.H. Mills, Box 506, Gaffney, South Carolina。在烟台停留约一个月后，莫拉索娃返回天津，住在牛津路的一家华人寄宿公寓。当她住在跑马厅路309号时，她与一位名叫福特的美国军医的妻子成为朋友，福特一家于1937年7月3日前往马尼拉。莫拉索娃继续与福特夫人通信，后来告诉他人说，福特夫人在马尼拉离婚，随后前往新加坡，并邀请她去同住一段时间。莫拉索娃多次表示打算去新加坡探望福特夫人。在天津逗留期间，莫拉索娃没有任何职业，但似乎总是资金充裕。正是在牛津路寄宿公寓居住期间，她结识了列兵罗斯林。在当地战事爆发初期，莫拉索娃非常紧张，不断表达她的恐惧（如果她确实为国家政治保卫总局工作，这是很容易理解的）。
1937年9月6日，她在俄国教堂与罗斯林结婚，未在领事馆登记，但在英军方面登记了全部细节。结婚时申报的年龄为25岁。婚后她毫不避讳地说，现在她无所畏惧了，因为她是英国臣民并持有英国护照，并公然吹嘘她嫁给罗斯林就是为了这个目的；即为了获得英国护照。
正如已知的那样，罗斯林夫人于11月/27日

page_data.en:
3.

27th November, 1937, for Shanghai on the pretext of visiting
relatives there. No money for her passage was given to her
by Rosling, who stated that he was always under the
impression that she had money hidden away in some bank
or other in Tientsin and that she could not possibly have
saved her passage money out of the allowances made to her.
The news from the Consulate-General at Manila stating that
she had reported the loss of her passport rather tends to
show that she was attempting to get to Singapore, and in
view of the foregoing I am afraid there is little doubt
that she is working for some person or other, probably the
Soviet Government, and her activities in that area will be
well worth watching.
